original_question: For which Fraisse classes with the strong amalgamation property (SAP) does the Fraisse limit have finite big Ramsey degrees? In particular, if such a class has finitely many relations and only finitely many forbidden substructures, or if all relations have arity at most two, must finite big Ramsey degrees always exist, and is there a general criterion characterizing exactly which SAP classes have this property?
target_in_paper: Section 6, Problem 6.1: "For which SAP Fraïssé classes does the Fraïssé limit have finite big Ramsey degrees?"
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's actual target. It correctly focuses on SAP Fraïssé classes, asks whether their Fraïssé limits have finite big Ramsey degrees, and it reproduces the three follow-up directions stated under Problem 6.1: the finitely many relations plus finite forbidden-substructure case, the additional arity-at-most-two restriction, and the search for a general criterion characterizing the SAP classes with this property.
missing_details: The paper's ambient setup is a Fraïssé class of finite structures in a finite relational language; this should be stated explicitly for the question to be stand-alone.
It should specify that the structure under study is the Fraïssé limit of the class, i.e. a countable homogeneous relational structure whose age is that class.

The phrase "has finite big Ramsey degrees" should be defined explicitly: for every finite substructure A of the Fraïssé limit, there is a finite bound T(A) such that every finite coloring of the copies of A has an isomorphic subcopy of the Fraïssé limit on which at most T(A) colors remain.

In the official wording of Problem 6.1, the arity-at-most-two clause is not an independent alternative hypothesis; it is a further restriction on the preceding case of SAP Fraïssé classes with finitely many relations and a finite set of forbidden substructures.

To stay faithful to the paper, the question should remain about existence of finite big Ramsey degrees, not drift into stronger neighboring questions about exact degree calculations, canonical partitions, or big Ramsey structures.

The paper itself uses the phrase "a finite set of forbidden substructures" in Problem 6.1 without replacing the problem by a narrower free-amalgamation Forb(F) formulation, so the refined version should preserve that scope rather than over-specify it.
refined_question: Let K be the Fraïssé limit of an SAP Fraïssé class of finite structures in a finite relational language. For which such classes does K have finite big Ramsey degrees, in the sense that for every finite substructure A of K there is a finite number T(A) such that every finite coloring of the copies of A in K has an isomorphic subcopy K' ≅ K on which at most T(A) colors appear? In particular, if the class has finitely many relation symbols and a finite set of forbidden substructures, must K have finite big Ramsey degrees; and, under those same hypotheses, if every relation symbol has arity at most two, do big Ramsey degrees always exist? Is there a general condition on SAP Fraïssé classes characterizing exactly those whose Fraïssé limits have finite big Ramsey degrees?
justification: The draft is targeting Section 6, Problem 6.1 almost verbatim. Its first sentence matches the headline open problem, and its follow-up clauses track the subquestions stated immediately after Problem 6.1. What it lacks is the Section 2 setup and the formal meaning of "finite big Ramsey degrees," as well as the important logical dependency that the binary-arity clause is a refinement of the finitely many relations plus finite forbidden-substructure case. The nearby Section 5 discussion confirms that this is the correct scope: by that point the paper has already identified broad positive classes, so Problem 6.1 asks for the larger SAP-level boundary of the theory.
